findings.title: forEach(async) in recurring-cancellation branch loses calendar deleteEvent calls
findings.body: In the recurring-cancellation branch (bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings) the code uses `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... })`. Array.prototype.forEach does not await async callbacks, so the inner `await getCalendar(credential)` and `await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` invocations are fire-and-forget and the pushes to `apiDeletes` happen asynchronously. By the time control reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652, `apiDeletes` will normally be empty for the recurring branch, so those `deleteEvent` calls are never awaited. Consequence: when an attendee (or organizer) cancels a recurring booking with `allRemainingBookings=true`, the response returns success but the underlying calendar events are not actually deleted on the external provider. Use `for (const credential of ...) { ... }` (as already done at lines 480-483 in the non-recurring branch) or `await Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map(...))` so the deletes are collected and awaited before the request resolves.

findings.title: forEach(async) in requestReschedule drops calendar/video cleanup
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` does not await its async callback, so the `await getCalendar(...)` + `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` and the `deleteMeeting(...)` calls for each booking reference are started but never awaited. The function then proceeds to send the reschedule email/webhook and returns to the client, meaning external calendar events and video meetings from the original booking are not reliably cleaned up when a booking is rescheduled. This was an existing latent issue (deleteEvent was already async) but the conversion to async `getCalendar` makes the missing await even more important. Replace the forEach with a for-of loop or Promise.all so all cleanup promises are awaited before returning.

findings.title: forEach(async) drops calendar cleanup on vital reschedule
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` does not await its callback. The `await getCalendar(credentialsMap.get(bookingRef.type))` and subsequent `calendar?.deleteEvent(bookingRef.uid, builder.calendarEvent)` invocations are untracked promises. The function returns `true` without waiting for these deletes, so a vital-related reschedule can complete without actually removing the previous calendar/video events on the external provider. The conversion from sync to async `getCalendar` makes this dependency concrete. Use `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { ... }` (with await inside) or wrap in `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`.

findings.title: forEach(async) drops calendar cleanup on wipemycalother reschedule
findings.body: Same pattern as in vital/lib/reschedule.ts: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` does not await its async callback, so the `await getCalendar(...)` + `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` calls run detached from the request lifecycle. The reschedule returns success without guaranteeing the prior calendar events are deleted. Use a sequential for-of or Promise.all to await the deletes before resolving.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns Promise<Calendar> but types still say Calendar
findings.body: `getCalendarCredentials` now constructs each `calendar` entry via `getCalendar(credential)`, which is async. The returned objects therefore have `calendar: Promise<Calendar | null>` at runtime, but there is no explicit return type or `.d.ts` update, so TypeScript still infers/asserts `calendar: Calendar | null`. This is an implicit API/contract break: any new or existing consumer that forgets to `await item.calendar` will call `.listCalendars()`/`.createEvent(...)`/`.deleteEvent(...)` on a Promise object and fail with a cryptic runtime error (e.g. `calendar.deleteEvent is not a function`). Either update the return type to reflect the Promise and rename the field (e.g. `calendarPromise`), or wrap the synchronous-style list construction with a single `Promise.all` inside `getCalendarCredentials` so callers see a real `Calendar` instance and existing call sites like `getConnectedCalendars` can drop their per-item await.

findings.title: Calendar deletes serialized by for-of instead of Promise.all
findings.body: The PR replaces the previous `forEach((credential) => { ... apiDeletes.push(calendar?.deleteEvent(...)); })` with a sequential `for (const credential of calendarCredentials) { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); apiDeletes.push(calendar?.deleteEvent(...)); }`. This now awaits each `getCalendar` and each `deleteEvent` one credential at a time. For users connected to many calendars (or with `_other_calendar` integrations) this serializes what used to run in parallel and noticeably slows cancellation latency. Preserve the new await-semantics but parallelize with `const calendars = await Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map(getCalendar)); apiDeletes.push(...calendars.map(c => c?.deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)));` (or equivalent `.flatMap`).

findings.title: Outer `calendar` variable unused after refactor
findings.body: `const calendar = await getCalendar(calendarCredential);` is now declared unconditionally but is only consumed in the `else` branch. In the `if (recurring && allRemainingBookings)` branch the code creates its own (shadowed) `calendar` inside the forEach callback, making the outer value dead. Either remove the outer declaration and move it into the `else` branch, or move the recurring-branch delete logic out so the outer calendar is actually used. As-is this is dead-await work and visual confusion about which calendar is being used.
